negative_reviews.author: Nabanita Talukdar
negative_reviews.text:
I am writing about an incident at the Aberdeen branch on 12 October 2026 at approximately 20:10, while working as a part-time delivery driver.

When I arrived, only two or three tables were occupied, yet the servers were gathered near the bar and I had to wait around 8–10 minutes just to get someone’s attention. When a server finally approached, I told him the order was ready and likely on the collection shelf. He checked the bag, insisted it was not the correct order, and walked away without properly resolving the issue.

I tried to get another server’s attention, but he also initially ignored me. When he eventually came forward, he likewise claimed the bag was incorrect and appeared reluctant to check it properly. I had to insist that he verify the order number before he finally acknowledged that it was the correct bag.

What disappointed me most was not simply the wasted time, but the lack of assistance, communication and professionalism throughout the interaction. Having several years of management experience myself, I understand that mistakes happen, but staff should be willing to check an order properly rather than dismissing a delivery driver who is simply trying to do their job.

Delivery drivers’ time matters too, and we should not have to repeatedly chase staff for basic assistance or insist on a straightforward order-number check.

I strongly encourage the management team to review this incident, including any available CCTV and order records, and address the staff conduct and collection procedures at this branch.

I hope management takes this feedback seriously and ensures that delivery drivers are treated with the courtesy and professionalism they deserve.

issues: Covers rose by 89 (4.9%) and spend per head by £0.02 week on week, but the £23 SPH target was missed.
Sales were £46,187.96, up £962.12 week on week and £4,187.96 (9.97%) above the £42,000 target.
Top sellers were Chicken Ramen (240), Steak Tataki Ramen (222) and Chicken Yakisoba (215); Yasai Set, Sea Bream Nigiri and Clam Nigiri sold once each.
All additionals fell slightly and the 10% drinks, 20% sushi and 13.5% sides targets were missed.
Operational labour was 20.49% (£9,512.14) against the 22% target, with 646.25 hours used and a FOH and BOH split of 46.1% and 53.9% against 45% and 55%.
Service was notably smooth after last week's rota changes; FOH and BOH agree the quality first rota is working, and there is room for extra kitchen labour for deep cleaning.
The budget rota is complete for the week commencing 19 October and drafted for the week commencing 26 October.
Food spend was 22.66% against the 25% target, with food and wet usage variance within the acceptable range.
Google reviews hit 80% against the 95% target: three 5 star, one 4 star and one 1 star from an unhappy delivery driver, which has been discussed with staff.
The new Deliverect is auto finishing orders within 4 minutes, so customers turn up for orders just placed; Inka is looking into it.
Staff are making mistakes with the new boxes because they cannot see inside, such as missing eggs, alongside higher Slerp volumes.
The book tour ticket cards had the wrong date and a box and a half were handed out; very few sold, but those customers need contacting.
Staffing: the handover to Elliot as Restaurant Manager is complete, and Joe is stepping down to part time supervisor after his last shift as GM on 21/10.

Esme has been hired as FOH supervisor and starts on Thursday, Rohit has been hired as part time FOH, and the kitchen management is being restructured with an assistant head chef role to promote Alberto.
BOH is stable, but sushi holidays in November need considering.
Compliance: pest control, fire, electrical, gas and ventilation completed.
Maintenance high priority: the emergency light on the ramen light is out, and the bar fridge handle and bar stock cupboard have come off (superglued only).

Other maintenance: heat lamps, the Kobas printer for the new Deliveroo scheme has still not arrived, the stock room is too hot, the bar fridge leaks intermittently, waiter stations 1 and 2 are coming away from the wall, and the light above the donburi.
The broken wall tiles behind the grease trap need a follow up with Kris, and the floor around the old grip taped areas needs repair, which can be done in house outside service hours.
The correct date stickers for the university frozen ramen promotion have arrived.
Deliveroo food quality, correct orders and the resulting reviews remain the area for improvement, though Deliveroo reviews look better again, and new review incentives are coming.
Halloween decorations and a dry ice cocktail need ordering.
Upcoming: Teddy's book tour, the app, the Deliveroo x Slerp promo, Deliveroo £7 off £15 orders, XOXO drinks, student frozen ramen and Deliverect.
Region: Rebecca reported a Scotland sales uptick from the school holidays (Admin Meeting 19/10).
Region: the 50% off and free ramen app vouchers end at the end of the month, while £5 ramen vouchers stay downloadable for new accounts in the short term and will be honoured (Admin Meeting 19/10).
Region: XOXO drinks move to the main menu and will no longer be tracked separately (Admin Meeting 19/10).
Region: 3,000 book copies have arrived at the office for distribution to sites by 12 November (Admin Meeting 19/10).
Region: digital Brix refractometers read well below manual tests (Maki 8 digital 5 against manual 6.5 to 7), so Michael mandated daily cleaning and calibration (Admin Meeting 19/10).
Region: incoming POS orders jumping straight to finished, delivered or preparing have been reported to Kobas and Deliverect, and Inka is changing the POS settings (Admin Meeting 19/10).
Region: a scalable beef solution is rolling out by the end of the month after product that did not match the approved specs was received (Admin Meeting 19/10).

Region: the factory sous vide chicken looked red because the recipe sheet used 3% soy instead of 1%; ingredients, taste, texture and slice size are approved, and restaurants sign off only once they see the finished, sliced and packed product (factory call 20/10).
Customers also complained that the new see through packaging makes portions look smaller (EDI/NEW KPI meeting 20/10).
Labour was skewed by higher sales, and the site is short of staff despite having hours available (EDI/NEW KPI meeting 20/10).
Compliance improved with iPad calendar alerts (EDI/NEW KPI meeting 20/10).
Aberdeen already uses the all in one iPad station with Hungry Panda and Slerp (EDI/NEW KPI meeting 20/10).
Region: GMs must attend the GM and head chef meeting in person or send a designated representative (EDI/NEW KPI meeting 20/10).
Region: all sites will move to recorded meetings (EDI/NEW KPI meeting 20/10).

Region: Michael plans to roll out the control centre dashboard to every site in the region over the next few days, with Rory guiding the other GMs; Ka Ho will confirm the rollout and logins with Michael on Wednesday (EDI/NEW KPI meeting 20/10).
Discounts cost about £3,500 (Penny thought about £4,000) (Scotland BOH KPI meeting 20/10).

Chef tour event on Sunday 15 November: both of the site's best sushi chefs are on long booked holiday that week, leaving one sushi chef and one trained team member for 40 teriyaki and 40 green dragon rolls; Matt will ask Teddy about extra support, possibly sending Ano (Scotland BOH KPI meeting 20/10).
The mango passion fruit mochi is to be confirmed as vegan, and the allergy sheet will be updated (Scotland BOH KPI meeting 20/10).

Lynas delivered only one of two cases of tonkotsu broth on 14/10 and the reorder was rebooked for 17/10 (£126.44 credit chased); coconut milk was missing on 16/10, and True World Fish was late on 13/10 (Scotland BOH KPI meeting 20/10).
Aberdeen cut its rider wait time dramatically within a week and is actively timing its processes, though rider wait is still amber (AM Updates 21/10).
The 1 star review came from a delivery driver about waiting at collection, which Ka Ho linked to sites marking orders ready too early; Elliot said it was not about the food (AM Updates 21/10).
Region: Michael made rider wait time the priority delivery metric this week, followed by ratings; sites need a 4.7 Deliveroo rating to compete and open times above 99.5% (AM Updates 21/10).
Region: GMs and head chefs must run a daily morning brief for FOH and BOH using the app's daily tab to review sales, delivery ratings and setups (AM Updates 21/10).

Region: failed delivery orders come from items marked out of stock on Kobas but not on Deliverect, so managers must update both, snooze unavailable extras by PLU and check Deliverect failed order statuses daily (AM Updates 21/10).

Region: stock edit permissions will be suspended for one week to see true variances, after wastage and comps were used to bring variances under 5% and distort Kobas ordering baselines (AM Updates 21/10).

Region: from next week automated Gemini meeting recordings and dashboard sign offs replace manual meeting notes and KPI sheets, with tasks synced to Asana and the legacy spreadsheets kept as a backup for now (AM Updates 21/10).
Region: third party discounted bookings are no longer allowed on Saturdays and are capped at a share of capacity on other days (AM Updates 21/10).

Region: Hungry Panda still has untranslated menu text, wrong integrations and overridden PLUs; Sophie is to fix the setup, and Michael suggested turning it off if it hurts Deliveroo and Slerp without enough revenue (AM Updates 21/10).
Region: ramen bowls are now ordered only from Harro, not Lynas (Scotland BOH KPI meeting 20/10).

Region: Teddy confirmed that during the app promotions sites may buy extra stock and ask Matt or Penny for extra kitchen hours, as the discounts are marketing for another 25,000 app sign ups (Scotland BOH KPI meeting 20/10).
Region: frozen ramen stock is limited and sites ran short last week, so Penny asked sites to check availability; no extra labour budget has been given for it (Scotland BOH KPI meeting 20/10).
Region: Lynas did not reply to any delivery issue report last week; 17 supplier issues across Scotland and Newcastle left £385.55 of credit due (Scotland BOH KPI meeting 20/10).
